body.statement: If \(D_{jh}=D_{jK}\) for every \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\), then \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}=W_{\mathrm{deep}}\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\).
body.justification: This exact reduction is a mandatory sanity check for designs without changing donor eligibility.
body.gap: The equality is implicit in any fixed-support formulation and pins down the boundary of the new width comparison.
body.consumer: Software regression tests can verify that enabling nested support leaves fixed-pool output unchanged when donor sets coincide.
body.proof_tex:
Assume that \(D_{jh}=D_{jK}\) for every \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  Fix \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  Equality of the supporting index sets gives equality of the corresponding simplexes,
\[
\Delta(D_{jh})=\Delta(D_{jK}).
\]
Taking the finite Cartesian product over \(e\in\mathcal E\) and using the construction of \(\mathcal F_s\) therefore yields
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jh})
=\prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jK})
=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{1}
\]

For clarity, let \(\mathcal B_s\) be the set of pairs \((w,\ell)\) that satisfy all constraints in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} for support rule \(s\).  In that definition the support-rule label occurs only through the requirement \(w\in\mathcal F_s\): the model class, estimator \(\widehat\tau(w)\), target \(\tau\), deterministic-width restriction, and uniform coverage event are otherwise the same for the two rules.  Consequently, (1) implies
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{nested}}=\mathcal B_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{2}
\]
The objective is the same map \((w,\ell)\mapsto\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e\) on both sets.  Applying the construction in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} to (2) gives, equation by equation,
\[
W_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{nested}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
=\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{deep}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
=W_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{3}
\]
This equality remains valid under the extended-value convention in the definition even if the common admissible set is empty.

Likewise, let \(\mathcal S_s\) denote the feasible set of tuples \((w,u,v,g)\) in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}.  The only support-rule-dependent constraint is \(w\in\mathcal F_s\).  All remaining constraints use the same fixed predictors, contrast-row map, covariance factor, constants, and coordinate set.  Hence (1) gives
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}=\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{4}
\]
Since both conic programs minimize the same scalar coordinate \(g\), (4) and \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} imply
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}}g
=\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}}g
=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (3) and (5) prove both asserted equalities.  No covariance rank, positivity, Gaussian, overlap, boundary, or limiting condition is used: the result follows solely from equality of the finite support-restricted feasible sets.
